tagline: Southeast from Page, with Earth Head on the horizon.
intro: SR 98 starts just south of Page, not far from the slot canyons of Antelope Canyon, and winds southeast across the Navajo Nation on changing grades toward US 160. Near the Page end, westbound drivers see Lake Powell, and for nearly the whole way Navajo Mountain sits on the horizon as a dome.
There is not much settlement. Hogans, shade houses and corrals show from the highway here and there, and near the south end Black Mesa comes into view, its strata left by a Cretaceous sea.

moments.title: Kaibeto
moments.text: Willow in the Water, in Navajo. The town grew up around springs, where runoff from White Mesa once watered corn and squash, and a trading post opened in 1914.

moments.title: Square Butte
moments.text: Entrada Sandstone towering more than 700 feet over the country beside the highway. The Navajo name means square rock, and it is.

moments.title: Navajo Mountain pullout
moments.text: The pullout at milepost 343 faces Naatsis'áán, Earth Head, 10,388 feet high and sacred to the Navajo, Hopi and Paiute.
